errors.claude-missing: Claude Code isn't installed or signed in on this computer. Set it up, then reopen this page.
errors.bad-request: The page sent something the app didn't expect. Reload the page and try again.
errors.forbidden: Only this app's own page can talk to your mini-me. Open it from the app's address.
errors.busy: Your mini-me is still working on something else. Try again in a moment.
errors.no-longer-waiting: This question is no longer waiting.
errors.not-in-office: You're not in an office yet.
errors.no-such-colleague: No one by that name is in the office.
errors.no-draft: Your mini-me couldn't write a draft. Try again, or write it yourself.
errors.relay-unreachable: Can't reach the relay. Whoever runs it may need to start it again.
errors.office-key-wrong: That office key doesn't open this office.
errors.office-member-unknown: The relay no longer knows your mini-me. Leave the office and join again.
errors.ai-busy: The AI service was busy. Try again a little later.
errors.timeout: It took too long and was stopped. Try again.
errors.learn-failed: I couldn't finish learning this time. Try again.
errors.fix-failed: I couldn't make that correction. Try again.
errors.import-failed: I couldn't read what you pasted. Try again.
errors.task-failed: I couldn't finish that. Try again, or ask it another way.
errors.nothing-to-read: I found nothing on this computer to learn from yet. Bring what your usual AI knows about you instead.
errors.flow-failed: The flow did not finish. Try Run now, or tell your mini-me what to change.
errors.too-many-tries: Too many wrong office keys from here. Try again in a few minutes.
errors.relay-failed: The relay ran into a problem. Try again.
errors.relay-port-taken: Another program is using the office's port on this computer. Close it and try again.
errors.messenger-token-wrong: Discord did not take that token. Copy it again from the Bot page.
errors.messenger-telegram-token-wrong: Telegram did not take that token. Copy it again from @BotFather; /token there gives a new one.
errors.messenger-telegram-taken: Another program reads this bot's messages too (Hermes Agent, for one), so they may not reach your mini-me. Stop it there, or make a new bot for your mini-me.
errors.messenger-slack-token-wrong: Slack did not take those tokens. Check the app-level token (xapp-, with connections:write) and the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-), and that the app was made from the manifest.
errors.messenger-refused: Discord stopped the bot. Check it in the Developer Portal and connect again.
errors.file-too-large: That file is larger than 25 MB, more than the office takes.
errors.files-too-many: Up to ten files go with one request.
errors.file-not-found: That file is not there any more.
errors.file-left-out: That file is in a folder you keep out, so it does not leave this computer.
errors.files-full: The office keeps no more files for now. Older ones go after two weeks.
errors.file-missing: That file is no longer at the office (files are kept two weeks).
errors.connector-needs-client: Google needs your team's OAuth client first.
errors.connector-unreachable: The service's sign-in could not be reached. Try again in a moment.
errors.connector-refused: The service did not accept it. Try connecting again.
errors.connector-expired: That sign-in was started too long ago. Connect again.
errors.connector-signed-out: The connection ran out. Connect again.
errors.connector-token: This one takes a personal token.
errors.connector-token-wrong: That does not look like a token.
errors.connector-client-wrong: That is not an OAuth client: give its client ID (and secret), or the JSON file.

firstRun.title: My mini-me
firstRun.hello: Hi, I'm your mini-me. To work the way you do, I first need to learn how you work. Here is how I'll learn.

read.title: What I read
read.body: What you asked your AI tools in the last 14 days, your AI instruction and memory files, the kinds of documents and apps you use, and your commits if you write code. For documents I see only the kind, never the contents or names.

keep.title: What I keep
keep.body: Only what will still be true in months — how you work, decide and talk — in five lines or fewer.

skip.title: What I don't keep
skip.body: Things that change, like projects, schedules and files. I look them up when I need them.

time.title: How long
time.body: About 30 seconds. It keeps going if you close this window.

firstRun.folders: These are the folders you worked in lately. Leave out any I shouldn't read.
firstRun.noFolders: I found no AI conversations on this computer. Bringing what your usual AI knows about you is the quickest start.
firstRun.foldersNote: I never read or search these folders. Leaving one out also removes what I had gathered from it for searching.

source.notes: Reading your AI instructions and memory files
source.inputs: Reading what you asked your AI tools lately
source.work: Looking at the kinds of documents and apps you use

firstRun.freshOffer: {count, plural, one {You've had # new conversation with your AI tools since I last read.} other {You've had # new conversations with your AI tools since I last read.}} Shall I see if there's anything new to learn?
firstRun.startOverSure: Move what I remember into a backup and start from the beginning? Nothing is deleted.
firstRun.tryNow: Shall we do one together now?
firstRun.startOverClear: Nothing you taught me is kept yet, only what I read from your records. Clear it and start from the beginning? Reading again brings it back.

memory.title: What I remember about you
memory.none: Nothing yet. I'll learn as we work together.
memory.where: Saved exactly like this in {dir} on this computer. Things that change aren't kept; I look them up when I need them.

import.while: While you wait, shall I bring what your usual AI knows about you?
import.step1: Copy this into a chat with the AI you use most, such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.
import.step2: Paste its answer here. I'll keep only what lasts, and the pasted text is not stored.
import.done: {count, plural, =0 {There was nothing new worth keeping.} one {I kept # line.} other {I kept # lines.}}

chat.carrying: This conversation is long: keeping what matters first, then summing up what came before
chat.carried: I summed up what came before and will go on from that.

office.title: Office
office.intro: Where your mini-me and your colleagues' trade requests. Your memory and conversations never go there; only cards and requests do.
office.name: Your name
office.role: What you do, in a line

office.nobody: No other mini-me yet. Send a colleague the invite link.

menu.title: Requests I take
menu.intro: What colleagues' mini-mes can bring you, and how much your mini-me does alone for each. Colleagues see the kinds, never how much it does alone.
menu.none: Nothing set yet. Once you set what you take, colleagues' mini-mes know what to bring you, and you decide for each kind whether your mini-me answers alone or asks you first.
menu.free: A request that fits none of these: your mini-me answers it and tells you.
menu.likeMe: Like you: {percent}%. In the last 30 days you sent {asIs} of the {total} answers I showed you first as they were.
menu.likeMeFew: In the last 30 days you sent {asIs} of the {total, plural, one {# answer} other {# answers}} I showed you first as {total, plural, one {it was} other {they were}}.

trustHint.ask: Shows you the answer first; it goes only when you say so

menu.name: What it is

flows.title: Flows
flows.intro: What your mini-me does on its own: at set times, or when a colleague's request comes in. A timed flow's answers go into a conversation of its own.
flows.none: None yet. Tell your mini-me, for example: “Every weekday at 9, sum up what is waiting for me,” or “When someone asks for a code review, have my web-app conversation look first.” It shows you the flow before making it.

when.inMinutes: Once, in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
when.invalid: Not a schedule it can keep: it would be refused.

suggest.morningAsk: Make a flow: every weekday at 9, catch me up in a few lines: what is waiting for my answer in the office, what came back from the requests I sent, and what I left open in my AI conversations since yesterday.
suggest.weekAsk: Make a flow: every Friday at 5 pm, list in a few lines what I finished this week and what is still open, from my AI conversations and my office requests.

flows.onRequest: Followed when such a request comes in
flows.tooLong: Too long to be kept (a name takes 80 characters, the request 4,000): it would be refused.

messenger.title: On your phone
messenger.intro: Talk with your mini-me from your phone, in Discord, Telegram or Slack, as you do here. It answers while this app runs on this computer, and what you say there shows here too.
messenger.step2: Paste the token here and connect.
messenger.asking: {name} wrote to your bot. Let them in only if their phone shows {code}.
messenger.paired: {bot} talks with {name} only. “/new” in {service, select, telegram {Telegram} slack {Slack} other {Discord}} starts a new conversation.
messenger.elsewhere: Another app on this computer is talking through this bot now.
messenger.knock: Almost there. Your mini-me is asking on your computer whether to let you in. Let yourself in there only if it shows {code}, and it answers what you wrote.
messenger.someoneWaiting: Someone else is already waiting to be let in here. If that is not you, press “Not them” on the computer, then write again.
messenger.taken: This mini-me already talks with someone else.
messenger.in: You are in. Write here and your mini-me answers. While you are away from its page, what needs you comes here too.
messenger.inHeld: You are in. Your mini-me answers what you wrote. While you are away from its page, what needs you comes here too.
messenger.busy: Still on your last message; I'll take this one next.
messenger.orReply: Or reply with your own words.
messenger.waiting: {count, plural, one {# question has} other {# questions have}} waited for you.
messenger.pushNote: While you are not looking at this page, what needs you comes to {service, select, telegram {Telegram} slack {Slack} other {Discord}}: questions about colleagues' requests, your flows' answers, and answers to what you asked. While your status says you are in a meeting, away or off, colleagues' questions wait and come together at 10, 14 and 17.

discord.step1: At Discord's Developer Portal, make a New Application. So nobody else can add it to a server, set Install Link to None on its Installation page and turn off Public Bot on its Bot page. There, press Reset Token and copy the token.
discord.tokenPlaceholder: The token from the Bot page
discord.step3: Add the bot to a server of your own: Discord only delivers a message to a bot you share a server with. A private server made for this is fine.
discord.addBot: Add the bot to a server
discord.step4: Send the bot a direct message, not in the server: on your phone, tap the bot in the server's member list, then Message. A question with a code appears here.

telegram.step1: In Telegram, open @BotFather and send /newbot. Give your bot a name, then a username that ends in “bot”. BotFather answers with its token; copy it.
telegram.step3: On your phone, open the chat with your bot and press Start. A question with a code appears here.
telegram.addBot: Open the chat with the bot
telegram.scan: Or point your phone's camera at this.

slack.step1: At api.slack.com/apps, choose Create New App, then From a manifest. Pick your workspace and paste this manifest; it asks only for what your mini-me uses.
slack.step2: Under Basic Information, App-Level Tokens: generate one with connections:write. It starts with xapp-.
slack.step3: Under Install App, install it to your workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token. It starts with xoxb-.
slack.step4: In Slack, open your app under Apps and write in its Messages tab. A question with a code appears here.
slack.scan: Or point your phone's camera at this.

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.intro: Let your mini-me work in Notion, Google, GitHub and more, through each service's own MCP server. It asks you before it uses one, until you let a kind of action go on alone. What you connect stays on this computer.
connectors.connecting: Approve it in the tab that opened…

does.gmail: Search and read mail, write drafts

google.title: Google
google.needsClient: Google wants an OAuth client registered for your team first. Someone on the team does it once in Google Cloud; then everyone connects their own account.
google.preview: Google's MCP servers are still in developer preview: whoever registers the client needs a Google Workspace account that joined Google's preview program.

steps.preview: With your Google Workspace account, join Google's <link>Workspace Developer Preview Program</link>. Google answers within a couple of days.
steps.apis: <link>Turn on the APIs</link> in a Google Cloud project (pick one or make one): Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs and Sheets, with their MCP servers.
steps.branding: In <link>Branding</link>, give the app a name such as sub-office; in <audience>Audience</audience>, choose Internal.
steps.scopes: In <link>Data Access</link>, press Add or remove scopes and paste these where it says Manually add scopes:
steps.client: <link>Create a client</link> of the type Desktop app, then press Download JSON.

google.webClient: A Web application client works too, with this address among its Authorized redirect URIs:
google.typeIt: Or type its client ID and secret
